nodes_add.name: Acharya Bhikshu
nodes_add.note: Founder of the Shvetambara Terapanth; left the Sthanakvasi group of Acharya Raghunath. Dates 1726-1803 (Wikipedia; Flügel, Jainpedia). Flügel's Jainpedia table dates his acharyaship from 1760.

nodes_add.name: Mahasi Sayadaw
nodes_add.note: Burmese monk (29 Jul 1904 - 14 Aug 1982, Wikipedia); resident teacher from 1947 at the Rangoon centre later called Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha (Thathana Yeiktha); teacher of Munindra and, via retreats at his centre, of Dipa Ma.

nodes_add.name: Joseph Goldstein
nodes_add.note: b. 20 May 1944 (Wikipedia); co-founded IMS, Barre, in 1975 with Kornfield and Salzberg; student of Dipa Ma per IMS and Lion's Roar.

nodes_add.name: Sharon Salzberg
nodes_add.note: b. 5 Aug 1952 (Wikipedia); co-founder of IMS (1975); student of Dipa Ma (Wikipedia, Lion's Roar).

nodes_add.name: Jack Kornfield
nodes_add.note: b. 1945; co-founder of IMS (1975); Dipa Ma was one of his teachers (Lion's Roar; IMS).

nodes_add.name: Niruben Amin (Niruma)
nodes_add.note: Doctor and disciple; led the Dada Bhagwan Foundation side of the 1988 split; succeeded by Deepakbhai Desai (Wikipedia citing Flugel 2005).

nodes_add.name: Kanubhai Patel
nodes_add.note: Early disciple and business partner of Dada Bhagwan; led the Jay Sachchidanand Sangh side of the 1988 split. Death June 2020 (9 June per Wikipedia only). A 2020 fraud complaint reported by News18 Gujarati could not be read or corroborated and is not in the profile.

nodes_update.note: One node for two men: Acharya Tulsi (20 Oct 1914 Ladnun - 23 Jun 1997 Gangasahar per JVBI) and Acharya Mahapragya (14 Jun 1920 Tamkor - 9 May 2010 Sardarshahar). Node born is Tulsi's birth and died is Mahapragya's death. Mahapragya was given the title 12 Nov 1978 and made yuvacharya 4 Feb 1979.

Ambalal Muljibhai Patel, b. 7 Nov 1908 Tarsali (Wikipedia citing Flügel, Jani, Wiley), d. 2 Jan 1988. Surat station experience June 1958 by his own account (Mahavideh Foundation booklet; Flügel abstract names Surat).
Nani Bala Barua, b. 25 Mar 1911 near Chittagong, d. 1 Sep 1989 Calcutta (Wikipedia; IMS and Lion's Roar give year only).
Anagarika Munindra; b. 1915 or 1914 (Wikipedia infobox vs its Tricycle citation) Chittagong, d. 14 Oct 2003 Igatpuri (Wikipedia); in Burma 1957-1966 as a close disciple of Mahasi Sayadaw.

glossary.def: "Small vow." The Terapanth movement, launched in 1949, that offers the five Jain monastic vows in reduced form to lay people of any religion.
"Meditation of perception." A Jain meditation system of eight parts, including breath and body perception, formulated by Mahapragya in 1975.
A Shvetambara Jain order founded by Acharya Bhikshu in the eighteenth century (his leadership dated from 1760), led by one acharya at a time; it does not worship images.
The five great vows of Jain monks and nuns: nonviolence, truth, not stealing, celibacy and non-possession.
"Stepless science." The movement founded by Dada Bhagwan, which offers knowledge of the Self through a ceremony instead of the step-by-step (kram) path.
The ceremony in Akram Vignan said to give direct knowledge of the Self.
In Jain belief a living tirthankara in the realm of Mahavideha; central to Akram Vignan.
"Insight." Buddhist meditation in which attention follows bodily and mental experience as it arises.
The Buddha's teaching, in its Pali form.

The brief's 'Critiques' section is not part of a profile, but the author may want one.

dipa-ma.mdx: Date 25 March 1911 and place of death Calcutta (1 Sep 1989) are Wikipedia only (flagged citation-needed elsewhere in that article); other sources give the year only. Siddhis in 1963 and the first stage of awakening are Wikipedia claims that conflict in places (Wikipedia places the Munindra meeting in 1963, Lion's Roar around her age 53, about 1964). Wikipedia's Barre dating (early 1980s) agrees with IMS (1980, 1984); a 1977 visit often cited elsewhere was not found.

Mahapragya b. 14 Jun 1920 Tamkor, d. 9 May 2010 Sardarshahar, name Mahapragya 12 Nov 1978, Yuvacharya 4 Feb 1979, handover 18 Feb 1994, installed 5 Feb 1995, preksha 1975, camps 1977, Jeevan Vigyan 28 Dec 1979, Ahimsa Yatra 2001-2009, quote 'Religion is beyond rituals.' -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mah%C4%81praj%C3%B1a

Initiated 29 Jan 1931; father died within weeks; chief secretary 1955; Tulsi asked him to investigate lost Jain meditation; 20 years of study; Anuvrat 1 Mar 1949 Sardarshahar -> https://www.jainology.org/end-of-an-era-acharya-mahapragyaji-passes-away/

Kanubhai received knowledge 1963; Simandhar Swami; split detail; Niruben's trusts; Trimandirs; police case, News18 March 2020, d. 9 Jun 2020; Flugel Jain-Vaishnava syncretism; discourses 1974-88 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akram_Vignan_Movement
Niruben b. 2 Dec 1944, d. 19 Mar 2006; Niruma from 1999; trusts; Deepakbhai Desai succession -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niruben_Amin

Marriage to Rajani Ranjan Barua, losses, husband's death, Munindra at about age 53, 1967 move, teaching content, five precepts, students -> https://www.lionsroar.com/mother-of-light-the-inspiring-story-of-dipa-ma/
